fixture_families.physical_intent: Repeat an already completed finishing pass on the same cylindrical surface without removing additional material.
fixture_families.oracle: At zero radial offset, every repeat after the first preserves the same physical material boundary and one connected retained body.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Remove a deliberately tiny radial layer whose depth sweeps across numerical and manufacturing tolerance scales.
fixture_families.oracle: Any strictly positive commanded depth is physical removal intent; the harness may separately classify whether a backend resolves it within its declared policy.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Move a turning envelope tangentially into an existing shoulder without a volumetric overlap at the limiting case.
fixture_families.oracle: The exact tangent member has no volumetric removal; signed offsets on either side distinguish clearance from real overlap.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Face exactly to a previously established end plane, including repeated facing passes at the same axial coordinate.
fixture_families.oracle: The zero-offset repeated face pass leaves the material set unchanged; negative/positive offsets bracket removal and clearance semantics.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Retrace already finished outside and inside cylindrical boundaries with fixed-axis tools.
fixture_families.oracle: Exact envelope retracing of the established OD or ID boundary must not invent removal, addition, or new bodies.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Bore to an existing internal shoulder so the cylindrical bore boundary meets the shoulder plane exactly or by a controlled signed offset.
fixture_families.oracle: The operation removes only intended bore material; exact plane meeting must neither leave a zero-thickness membrane nor over-cut the shoulder.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Traverse an engaged finishing path and immediately reverse along the same path without additional intended stock removal on the return.
fixture_families.oracle: Once the forward pass establishes the surface, exact reverse traversals preserve the same material set.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Represent natural analogue-control jitter around a nominal cylindrical finishing feed without turning sampling noise into arbitrary topology.
fixture_families.oracle: Material removal follows the canonicalized envelope within declared trajectory bounds; connectivity remains one retained body.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Apply a very long sequence of mostly redundant finishing operations to test operation-count scaling and topology stability.
fixture_families.oracle: Only distinct deeper envelopes change material; redundant repeats must not multiply physical boundaries or alter retained-body connectivity.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Part completely through a cylindrical workpiece so retained material becomes two disconnected volumetric bodies before any user-facing scrap policy is applied.
fixture_families.oracle: At complete cut-through the material set contains two disconnected bodies; neither body may be silently discarded by fixture semantics.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Move a cutter envelope exactly along an already machined edge with signed lateral offsets around the coincidence case.
fixture_families.oracle: The exact coincident member performs no new volumetric removal; neighboring offsets bracket overlap versus clearance.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Sweep a face mill or end mill exactly across an already established planar face.
fixture_families.oracle: At zero offset the sweep is coplanar with the existing face and does not change the volumetric material set.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Enter and leave a workpiece tangentially at a corner while sweeping signed offsets around exact contact.
fixture_families.oracle: Exact tangent contact alone removes no volume; penetrative members remove material and clearance members do not.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Repeat exactly the same slot trajectory and cutter envelope after the first slot is complete.
fixture_families.oracle: After the first completed slot, exact repeats leave the material set unchanged and must not grow topology without bound.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Cut partially and fully overlapping slots or pockets so later removals reuse substantial portions of earlier boundaries.
fixture_families.oracle: The final material equals stock minus the union of cutter envelopes; redundant overlap must not create duplicate physical boundaries.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Leave a deliberately small but volumetric cusp between neighboring cutter passes and sweep cusp size through tolerance scales.
fixture_families.oracle: A positive-volume cusp is material unless a later explicit regularization/export policy intentionally removes it within declared bounds.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Sweep a fixed-orientation cutter along a self-crossing freehand XYZ trajectory, creating repeated local envelope overlaps.
fixture_families.oracle: Removal equals the swept cutter-volume union over the canonical trajectory, independent of path self-crossing multiplicity.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Retrace an already cut path with bounded analogue jitter to separate legitimate tiny extra removal from sampling noise and exact repeats.
fixture_families.oracle: Zero-jitter retrace changes no material; nonzero jitter may remove bounded additional material according to the canonical trajectory.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Plunge a cutter by a deliberately tiny positive depth through numerical and manufacturing tolerance scales.
fixture_families.oracle: Any strictly positive commanded plunge expresses volumetric removal intent, even if a backend later reports it below a configured resolution threshold.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Exercise cutter/workpiece contact that is exactly point-only, edge-only, or face-only without volumetric overlap.
fixture_families.oracle: Pure lower-dimensional contact at zero offset removes no volume; signed offsets distinguish penetration and clearance.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Machine a through-slot that fully disconnects the stock into separate volumetric material bodies.
fixture_families.oracle: At complete cut-through the physical result contains two disconnected material bodies, both of which remain represented until an explicit later selection policy acts.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Apply an extremely dense canonical trajectory whose geometric envelope remains simple enough to detect representation-driven topology or runtime explosion.
fixture_families.oracle: The resulting physical removal follows the same bounded trajectory envelope regardless of segmentation density; segmentation alone must not change intended topology.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Exercise exact coincident and coplanar volumetric boundaries independent of a specific process solver.
fixture_families.oracle: The zero-offset/zero-angle member establishes exact coincidence; neighboring members expose whether observed changes are geometric or tolerance-policy effects.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Create a controlled positive overlap volume between analytic solids and sweep the overlap thickness through small scales.
fixture_families.oracle: Strictly positive overlap is real volumetric intersection; the intended result is not the same as the exact-contact member.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Classify exact point, edge, and face contacts between closed volumetric material regions without positive-volume overlap.
fixture_families.oracle: Zero-thickness contact is not volumetric fusion or removal; connectivity semantics are recorded separately from Boolean success.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Create a valid positive-volume sliver whose smallest dimension spans many orders of magnitude.
fixture_families.oracle: The sliver remains physical material while its volume is positive; backend cleanup may only remove it under an explicit bounded policy.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Apply a chain of individually small transformations or removals whose aggregate displacement is measurable and should not be hidden by local tolerance decisions.
fixture_families.oracle: Aggregate intended displacement/removal equals the explicit operation sequence; no global epsilon may silently erase accumulated intent without declaring that policy.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Repeat overlapping removals whose final material boundary is simple relative to the number of operations, exposing needless topology growth.
fixture_families.oracle: Physical boundary complexity follows the union of distinct removal envelopes rather than the raw number of repeated operations.

fixture_families.physical_intent: Sweep a separating cut parameter from connected material through the exact cut-through threshold to disconnected bodies.
fixture_families.oracle: Positive remaining bridge is one connected material body; complete removal crosses to multiple disconnected bodies without silently dropping either side.

lifecycle.minimization: Retain the original manufacturing trace or family member, create a separate minimized reproducer, and preserve the physical-intent oracle, parameter values, units/frame, tolerance-policy reference and connectivity semantics.
lifecycle.regression: Backend observations are append-only result records keyed by corpus version, family id, revision, parameter tuple, backend/version and policy configuration; a backend result never rewrites expected physical intent.
lifecycle.versioning: Changing intent, parameter domains, expected classification, units/frames or tolerance semantics requires a new family revision or corpus version; published benchmark result records continue to reference the exact prior version.
